name: Isaiah
tagline: Judgment, comfort, and the coming servant
author: Isaiah son of Amoz. Some scholars see later editing, while others hold to a single author.
date: Isaiah’s ministry ran from about 740 to 700 BC.
setting: Judah under threat from Assyria, and later the promise of comfort for exiles.
theme: God judges sin and promises salvation through a coming king and suffering servant.

outline.label: The LORD’s case against his people
Babylon, Moab, Egypt, Tyre, and others

christInBook: Isaiah speaks of a virgin’s son called Immanuel (7:14), a child who is Mighty God (9:6), a branch from Jesse (11:1), a servant who bears our sins (52:13-53:12), and a herald who brings good news (61:1). The New Testament quotes the book more than any other prophet.
howToRead: Isaiah alternates between judgment and hope. Watch for the Holy One of Israel, a title that appears throughout. The book is a unified message of sin, judgment, comfort, and a new creation.
